I analyze divergence between independent signals to detect coercion where actors involved can manipulate what data is recorded. Previous cases include a single agroindustrial firm in coastal Honduras, the national government of Afghanistan, opium cultivation under competing armed groups in northern Myanmar, and soil degradation along a displacement corridor in eastern Cameroon.

Since 2015 I've worked across Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the American South in teaching, social work, manual labor, and program design. Among others these include co-founding a teacher-training program in Egypt (2017–present) and developing cybersecurity curricula and training for USAID in Kazakhstan (2021). Hablo español.
